text:
The year was 1889, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world.

The city was Paris, the country known for the Eiffel Tower, where the iron lattice of the new tower pierced the sky, casting a long shadow over the remaining green spaces. Eli watched as the smoke from the factories mingled with the morning mist, a stark contrast to the vibrant life surrounding him. He knew that the preservation of this grove was not just about saving trees, but about saving a piece of the soul of the world from the relentless march of progress.
